sanskrit: kārttikyām adya bhoktāraḥ sahasraṃ me dvijottamāḥ tatrāyam api bhoktā vai deyam asmai ca me dhanam
english: "On this day of the full moon of Kārttika a thousand of the finest twice-born shall dine with me; among them this man too shall eat, and to him I shall give wealth."

sanskrit: tataḥ sahasraṃ viprāṇāṃ viduṣāṃ samalaṃkṛtam snātānām anusaṃprāptam ahatakṣaumavāsasām
english: Then a thousand brāhmaṇas, learned and finely adorned, freshly bathed and clad in unworn linen garments, arrived together.

sanskrit: tān āgatān dvijaśreṣṭhān virūpākṣo viśāṃ pate yathārhaṃ pratijagrāha vidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā
english: As those foremost of the twice-born came, O lord of peoples, Virūpākṣa received each according to his due with rites prescribed by ordinance.

sanskrit: bṛsyas teṣāṃ tu saṃnyastā rākṣasendrasya śāsanāt bhūmau varakuthāstīrṇāḥ preṣyair bharatasattama
english: By command of the lord of the rākṣasas seats of grass were laid out for them, spread with choice coverlets upon the ground by his servants, O best of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: tāsu te pūjitā rājñā niṣaṇṇā dvijasattamāḥ vyarājanta mahārāja nakṣatrapatayo yathā
english: Honored by the king and seated upon them, those most excellent of the twice-born shone forth, O great king, like the lords of the constellations.

sanskrit: tato jāmbūnadāḥ pātrīr vajrāṅkā vimalāḥ śubhāḥ varānnapūrṇā viprebhyaḥ prādān madhughṛtāplutāḥ
english: Then he gave to the brāhmaṇas vessels of fine gold, marked with diamonds, spotless and lovely, brimming with choice food drenched in honey and clarified butter.

sanskrit: tasya nityaṃ tathāṣāḍhyāṃ māghyāṃ ca bahavo dvijāḥ īpsitaṃ bhojanavaraṃ labhante satkṛtaṃ sadā
english: At his court, ever on the full moon of Āṣāḍha and of Māgha, many twice-born regularly received the choicest fare they desired, always with honor.

sanskrit: viśeṣatas tu kārttikyāṃ dvijebhyaḥ saṃprayacchati śaradvyapāye ratnāni paurṇamāsyām iti śrutiḥ
english: But on the full moon of Kārttika in particular, at the close of autumn, he bestowed jewels upon the twice-born—so the sacred report has it—on that day of the full moon.

sanskrit: suvarṇaṃ rajataṃ caiva maṇīn atha ca mauktikam vajrān mahādhanāṃś caiva vaiḍūryājinarāṅkavān
english: Gold and silver, gems and pearls, and diamonds of great worth, lapis lazuli, hides, and woolen rugs—

sanskrit: ratnarāśīn vinikṣipya dakṣiṇārthe sa bhārata tataḥ prāha dvijaśreṣṭhān virūpākṣo mahāyaśāḥ
english: having heaped up these masses of treasure to serve as priestly gifts, O Bhārata, the far-famed Virūpākṣa then spoke to those foremost of the twice-born:

sanskrit: gṛhṇīta ratnāny etāni yathotsāhaṃ yatheṣṭataḥ yeṣu yeṣu ca bhāṇḍeṣu bhuktaṃ vo dvijasattamāḥ tāny evādāya gacchadhvaṃ svaveśmānīti bhārata
english: "Take these jewels, according to your wish and as much as your eagerness allows; and whatever vessels you have eaten from, O most excellent of the twice-born, take those very vessels too and depart to your own homes," O Bhārata.

sanskrit: ity uktavacane tasmin rākṣasendre mahātmani yatheṣṭaṃ tāni ratnāni jagṛhur brāhmaṇarṣabhāḥ
english: When that high-souled lord of the rākṣasas had spoken these words, those bulls among brāhmaṇas took up the jewels as they pleased.

sanskrit: tato mahārhais te sarve ratnair abhyarcitāḥ śubhaiḥ brāhmaṇā mṛṣṭavasanāḥ suprītāḥ sma tadābhavan
english: Then, all honored with those costly and beautiful jewels, the brāhmaṇas in their spotless garments became greatly content.

sanskrit: tatas tān rākṣasendraś ca dvijān āha punar vacaḥ nānādigāgatān rājan rākṣasān pratiṣidhya vai
english: Then the lord of the rākṣasas, having restrained the rākṣasas who had come from every quarter, O king, again addressed those twice-born with these words:

sanskrit: adhyaikadivasaṃ viprā na vo 'stīha bhayaṃ kva cit rākṣasebhyaḥ pramodadhvam iṣṭato yāta māciram
english: "For this one day, O brāhmaṇas, you have nothing whatever to fear here from the rākṣasas. Rejoice, and go where you please without delay."

sanskrit: tataḥ pradudruvuḥ sarve viprasaṃghāḥ samantataḥ gautamo 'pi suvarṇasya bhāram ādāya satvaraḥ
english: Then all the throngs of brāhmaṇas hastened away in every direction; and Gautama too, taking up a load of gold, set out in haste.

sanskrit: kṛcchrāt samudvahan vīra nyagrodhaṃ samupāgamat nyaṣīdac ca pariśrāntaḥ klāntaś ca kṣudhitaś ca ha
english: Bearing it with much labor, O hero, he came to a banyan tree and sat down, worn out, weary, and hungry.

sanskrit: tatas tam abhyagād rājan rājadharmā khagottamaḥ svāgatenābhyanandac ca gautamaṃ mitravatsalaḥ
english: Then, O king, Rājadharman, that finest of birds, came up to him and, fond of his friend, welcomed Gautama with greetings of "You are welcome."

sanskrit: tasya pakṣāgravikṣepaiḥ klamaṃ vyapanayat khagaḥ pūjāṃ cāpy akarod dhīmān bhojanaṃ cāpy akalpayat
english: By the fanning of his wing-tips the bird drove away his fatigue; and the wise one paid him honor and made ready food for him as well.

sanskrit: sa bhuktavān suviśrānto gautamo 'cintayat tadā hāṭakasyābhirūpasya bhāro 'yaṃ sumahān mayā gṛhīto lobhamohād vai dūraṃ ca gamanaṃ mama
english: Having eaten and well rested, Gautama then reflected: "This is a very great load of fine gold that I have taken up out of greed and delusion, and my journey is far.

sanskrit: na cāsti pathi bhoktavyaṃ prāṇasaṃdhāraṇaṃ mama kiṃ kṛtvā dhārayeyaṃ vai prāṇān ity abhyacintayat
english: And there is nothing on the road to eat that might sustain my life. By what means, then, might I keep my life going?"—so he pondered.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa pathi bhoktavyaṃ prekṣamāṇo na kiṃ cana kṛtaghnaḥ puruṣavyāghra manasedam acintayat
english: Then, seeing nothing whatever along the road to eat, that ingrate, O tiger among men, thought this within his mind:

sanskrit: ayaṃ bakapatiḥ pārśve māṃsarāśiḥ sthito mama imaṃ hatvā gṛhītvā ca yāsye 'haṃ samabhidrutam
english: "This lord of cranes stands at my side, a very heap of flesh. Having killed him and taken him, I shall go on my way in all haste."

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atha tatra mahārciṣmān analo vātasārathiḥ tasyāvidūre rakṣārthaṃ khagendreṇa kṛto 'bhavat
english: Bhīṣma said: Now a great blazing fire, with the wind for its charioteer, had been kindled there nearby by the lord of birds for his protection.

sanskrit: sa cāpi pārśve suṣvāpa viśvasto bakarāṭ tadā kṛtaghnas tu sa duṣṭātmā taṃ jighāṃsur ajāgarat
english: And the king of cranes too slept trustingly at his side; but that ingrate, the wicked-souled one, eager to slay him, lay awake.

sanskrit: tato 'lātena dīptena viśvastaṃ nijaghāna tam nihatya ca mudā yuktaḥ so 'nubandhaṃ na dṛṣṭavān
english: Then with a blazing firebrand he struck down the trusting bird; and having slain him, filled with glee, he did not foresee the consequence.

sanskrit: sa taṃ vipakṣaromāṇaṃ kṛtvāgnāv apacat tadā taṃ gṛhītvā suvarṇaṃ ca yayau drutataraṃ dvijaḥ
english: Having plucked him bare of feathers, he cooked him then upon the fire; and taking both the bird and the gold, the brāhmaṇa went away in greater haste.

sanskrit: tato 'nyasmin gate cāhni virūpākṣo 'bravīt sutam na prekṣe rājadharmāṇam adya putra khagottamam
english: Then, when the next day had come, Virūpākṣa said to his son: "I do not see Rājadharman today, my son, that finest of birds.

sanskrit: sa pūrvasaṃdhyāṃ brahmāṇaṃ vandituṃ yāti sarvadā māṃ cādṛṣṭvā kadā cit sa na gacchati gṛhān khagaḥ
english: He always goes at the morning twilight to pay homage to Brahmā, and never once does that bird go to his home without first seeing me.

sanskrit: ubhe dvirātraṃ saṃdhye vai nābhyagāt sa mamālayam tasmān na śudhyate bhāvo mama sa jñāyatāṃ suhṛt
english: For two nights now, at both twilights, he has not come to my dwelling; therefore my heart is not at ease. Let it be learned how that friend fares.

sanskrit: svādhyāyena viyukto hi brahmavarcasavarjitaḥ taṃ gatas tatra me śaṅkā hanyāt taṃ sa dvijādhamaḥ
english: That basest of the twice-born, bereft of his sacred recitation and void of brahmanic luster—I fear that, having gone to him there, he may have slain him.

sanskrit: durācāras tu durbuddhir iṅgitair lakṣito mayā niṣkriyo dāruṇākāraḥ kṛṣṇo dasyur ivādhamaḥ
english: Of evil conduct and evil mind, I marked him by his gestures—idle, of cruel aspect, swarthy, base as a marauding outlaw.

sanskrit: gautamaḥ sa gatas tatra tenodvignaṃ mano mama putra śīghram ito gatvā rājadharmaniveśanam jñāyatāṃ sa viśuddhātmā yadi jīvati māciram
english: That Gautama has gone there, and at that my mind is troubled. My son, go swiftly from here to Rājadharman's abode, and let it be learned whether that pure-souled one yet lives—and waste no time."

sanskrit: sa evam uktas tvarito rakṣobhiḥ sahito yayau nyagrodhaṃ tatra cāpaśyat kaṅkālaṃ rājadharmaṇaḥ
english: Thus addressed, he went in haste, accompanied by rākṣasas, and there at the banyan tree he beheld the skeleton of Rājadharman.

sanskrit: sa rudann agamat putro rākṣasendrasya dhīmataḥ tvaramāṇaḥ paraṃ śaktyā gautamagrahaṇāya vai
english: Weeping, the son of the wise lord of the rākṣasas went on, hastening with all his might to seize Gautama.

sanskrit: tato 'vidūre jagṛhur gautamaṃ rākṣasās tadā rājadharmaśarīraṃ ca pakṣāsthicaraṇojjhitam
english: Then, not far off, the rākṣasas seized Gautama, and with him the body of Rājadharman, stripped of its wings, bones, and feet.

sanskrit: tam ādāyātha rakṣāṃsi drutaṃ meruvrajaṃ yayuḥ rājñaś ca darśayām āsuḥ śarīraṃ rājadharmaṇaḥ kṛtaghnaṃ puruṣaṃ taṃ ca gautamaṃ pāpacetasam
english: Taking him up, the rākṣasas went swiftly to the dwelling on Meru and showed the king the body of Rājadharman, and that ungrateful man Gautama of sinful mind.

sanskrit: ruroda rājā taṃ dṛṣṭvā sāmātyaḥ sapurohitaḥ ārtanādaś ca sumahān abhūt tasya niveśane
english: At the sight the king wept, together with his ministers and his household priest, and a very great cry of anguish arose in his dwelling.

sanskrit: sastrīkumāraṃ ca puraṃ babhūvāsvasthamānasam athābravīn nṛpaḥ putraṃ pāpo 'yaṃ vadhyatām iti
english: The whole city, with its women and children, grew sick at heart; and the king said to his son, "Let this evildoer be put to death."

sanskrit: asya māṃsair ime sarve viharantu yatheṣṭataḥ pāpācāraḥ pāpakarmā pāpātmā pāpaniścayaḥ hantavyo 'yaṃ mama matir bhavadbhir iti rākṣasāḥ
english: "Let all these feast upon his flesh at their pleasure. Of evil conduct, evil deeds, evil soul, and evil resolve, this man is to be slain—such is my judgment, O rākṣasas; let it be carried out by you."

sanskrit: ity uktā rākṣasendreṇa rākṣasā ghoravikramāḥ naicchanta taṃ bhakṣayituṃ pāpakarmāyam ity uta
english: Thus addressed by the lord of the rākṣasas, the rākṣasas of dreadful prowess did not wish to devour him, saying, "This man is a doer of evil."

sanskrit: dasyūnāṃ dīyatām eṣa sādhv adya puruṣādhamaḥ ity ūcus taṃ mahārāja rākṣasendraṃ niśācarāḥ
english: "It were well that this basest of men be given over to the outlaws this very day"—so, O great king, the night-roamers said to the lord of the rākṣasas.

sanskrit: śirobhiś ca gatā bhūmim ūcū rakṣogaṇādhipam na dātum arhasi tvaṃ no bhakṣaṇāyāsya kilbiṣam
english: And touching the ground with their heads, they said to the lord of the rākṣasa hosts: "You ought not to give us this sinner to eat."

sanskrit: evam astv iti tān āha rākṣasendro niśācarān dasyūnāṃ dīyatām eṣa kṛtaghno 'dyaiva rākṣasāḥ
english: "So be it," the lord of the rākṣasas said to those night-roamers; "let this ingrate be given over to the outlaws this very day, O rākṣasas."

sanskrit: ity ukte tasya te dāsāḥ śūlamudgarapāṇayaḥ chittvā taṃ khaṇḍaśaḥ pāpaṃ dasyubhyaḥ pradadus tadā
english: When this was said, his servants, spears and maces in hand, cut that sinner into pieces and then gave him over to the outlaws.

sanskrit: dasyavaś cāpi naicchanta tam attuṃ pāpakāriṇam kravyādā api rājendra kṛtaghnaṃ nopabhuñjate
english: But the outlaws too did not wish to eat that doer of evil; even flesh-eating beasts, O lord of kings, do not feed upon an ingrate.

sanskrit: brahmaghne ca surāpe ca core bhagnavrate tathā niṣkṛtir vihitā rājan kṛtaghne nāsti niṣkṛtiḥ
english: For the slayer of a brāhmaṇa, the drinker of liquor, the thief, and the breaker of vows, an expiation is ordained, O king; but for the ingrate there is no expiation.

sanskrit: mitradrohī nṛśaṃsaś ca kṛtaghnaś ca narādhamaḥ kravyādaiḥ kṛmibhiś cānyair na bhujyante hi tādṛśāḥ
english: The betrayer of a friend, the cruel man, and the ingrate—basest of men—such men are not fed upon even by carrion-beasts, by worms, or by any other creatures.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tataś citāṃ bakapateḥ kārayām āsa rākṣasaḥ ratnair gandhaiś ca bahubhir vastraiś ca samalaṃkṛtām
english: Bhīṣma said: Then the rākṣasa had a funeral pyre made ready for the lord of cranes, adorned with jewels, with many perfumes, and with garments.

sanskrit: tatra prajvālya nṛpate bakarājaṃ pratāpavān pretakāryāṇi vidhivad rākṣasendraś cakāra ha
english: Having there set the king of cranes ablaze, O king, the mighty lord of the rākṣasas performed the funeral rites in due form.

sanskrit: tasmin kāle 'tha surabhir devī dākṣāyaṇī śubhā upariṣṭāt tatas tasya sā babhūva payasvinī
english: At that very moment the goddess Surabhi, lovely daughter of Dakṣa, appeared above him, abounding in milk.

sanskrit: tasyā vaktrāc cyutaḥ phenaḥ kṣīramiśras tadānagha so 'patad vai tatas tasyāṃ citāyāṃ rājadharmaṇaḥ
english: From her mouth there fell foam mingled with milk, O sinless one, and it dropped upon that pyre of Rājadharman.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃjīvitas tena bakarājas tadānagha utpatya ca sameyāya virūpākṣaṃ bakādhipaḥ
english: By this the king of cranes was restored to life, O sinless one, and the lord of cranes, springing up, came to meet Virūpākṣa.

sanskrit: tato 'bhyayād devarājo virūpākṣapuraṃ tadā prāha cedaṃ virūpākṣaṃ diṣṭyāyaṃ jīvatīty uta
english: Then the king of the gods came to Virūpākṣa's city and said this to Virūpākṣa: "By good fortune this one lives!"

sanskrit: śrāvayām āsa cendras taṃ virūpākṣaṃ purātanam yathā śāpaḥ purā datto brahmaṇā rājadharmaṇaḥ
english: And Indra made known to Virūpākṣa the ancient tale—how a curse had once been laid upon Rājadharman by Brahmā:

sanskrit: yadā bakapatī rājan brahmāṇaṃ nopasarpati tato roṣād idaṃ prāha bakendrāya pitāmahaḥ
english: When once, O king, the lord of cranes failed to approach Brahmā, the Grandsire in anger spoke this to the lord of cranes:

sanskrit: yasmān mūḍho mama sado nāgato 'sau bakādhamaḥ tasmād vadhaṃ sa duṣṭātmā nacirāt samavāpsyati
english: "Since that base crane in his folly has not come to my assembly, therefore that wicked-souled one shall meet his death before long."

sanskrit: tadāyaṃ tasya vacanān nihato gautamena vai tenaivāmṛtasiktaś ca punaḥ saṃjīvito bakaḥ
english: So it was that, by that word, this crane was slain by Gautama; and by that same word, sprinkled with the nectar, he was restored to life again.

sanskrit: rājadharmā tataḥ prāha praṇipatya puraṃdaram yadi te 'nugrahakṛtā mayi buddhiḥ puraṃdara sakhāyaṃ me sudayitaṃ gautamaṃ jīvayety uta
english: Then Rājadharman, bowing before Purandara, said: "If your mind is set on showing me favor, O Purandara, then restore to life my dear, beloved friend Gautama."

sanskrit: tasya vākyaṃ samājñāya vāsavaḥ puruṣarṣabha saṃjīvayitvā sakhye vai prādāt taṃ gautamaṃ tadā
english: Heeding his words, Vāsava, O bull among men, brought Gautama back to life and gave him then to his friend.

sanskrit: sabhāṇḍopaskaraṃ rājaṃs tam āsādya bakādhipaḥ saṃpariṣvajya suhṛdaṃ prītyā paramayā yutaḥ
english: O king, the lord of cranes, coming upon him with his vessels and his goods, embraced his friend, filled with the highest affection.

sanskrit: atha taṃ pāpakarmāṇaṃ rājadharmā bakādhipaḥ visarjayitvā sadhanaṃ praviveśa svam ālayam
english: Then Rājadharman, lord of cranes, having sent away that doer of evil deeds together with his wealth, entered his own abode.

sanskrit: yathocitaṃ ca sa bako yayau brahmasadas tadā brahmā ca taṃ mahātmānam ātithyenābhyapūjayat
english: And the crane, as was fitting, then went to the assembly of Brahmā; and Brahmā honored that high-souled one with the rites of hospitality.

sanskrit: gautamaś cāpi saṃprāpya punas taṃ śabarālayam śūdrāyāṃ janayām āsa putrān duṣkṛtakāriṇaḥ
english: And Gautama too, returning again to that dwelling of the Śabaras, begot upon his Śūdra woman sons who became doers of evil.

sanskrit: śāpaś ca sumahāṃs tasya dattaḥ suragaṇais tadā kukṣau punarbhvāṃ bhāryāyāṃ janayitvā cirāt sutān nirayaṃ prāpsyati mahat kṛtaghno 'yam iti prabho
english: And a most grievous curse was then laid upon him by the hosts of the gods: "Having begotten sons after long delay in the womb of his remarried wife, this ingrate shall at last attain a great hell," O lord.

sanskrit: etat prāha purā sarvaṃ nārado mama bhārata saṃsmṛtya cāpi sumahad ākhyānaṃ puruṣarṣabha mayāpi bhavate sarvaṃ yathāvad upavarṇitam
english: All this Nārada told me long ago, O Bhārata, recalling that very great tale; and I too, O bull among men, have recounted the whole of it to you just as it was.

sanskrit: kutaḥ kṛtaghnasya yaśaḥ kutaḥ sthānaṃ kutaḥ sukham aśraddheyaḥ kṛtaghno hi kṛtaghne nāsti niṣkṛtiḥ
english: Whence is there glory for an ingrate, whence a standing, whence happiness? For the ingrate is not to be trusted; for the ingrate there is no expiation.

sanskrit: mitradroho na kartavyaḥ puruṣeṇa viśeṣataḥ mitradhruṅ nirayaṃ ghoram anantaṃ pratipadyate
english: The betrayal of a friend should never be done by any man; the betrayer of a friend attains a dreadful and endless hell.

sanskrit: kṛtajñena sadā bhāvyaṃ mitrakāmena cānagha mitrāt prabhavate satyaṃ mitrāt prabhavate balam satkārair uttamair mitraṃ pūjayeta vicakṣaṇaḥ
english: One should ever be grateful and desirous of friends, O sinless one; from a friend springs truth, from a friend springs strength. The discerning man should honor a friend with the highest marks of respect.

sanskrit: parityājyo budhaiḥ pāpaḥ kṛtaghno nirapatrapaḥ mitradrohī kulāṅgāraḥ pāpakarmā narādhamaḥ
english: The wise should wholly forsake the sinful ingrate, the shameless one, the betrayer of friends—a disgrace to his line, a doer of evil deeds, basest of men.

sanskrit: eṣa dharmabhṛtāṃ śreṣṭha proktaḥ pāpo mayā tava mitradrohī kṛtaghno vai kiṃ bhūyaḥ śrotum icchasi
english: Thus, O best of the upholders of dharma, I have declared to you this sinner, the betrayer of friends, the ingrate. What more do you wish to hear?

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca etac chrutvā tadā vākyaṃ bhīṣmeṇoktaṃ mahātmanā yudhiṣṭhiraḥ prītamanā babhūva janamejaya
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Hearing these words then spoken by the high-souled Bhīṣma, Yudhiṣṭhira became glad at heart, O Janamejaya.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca dharmāḥ pitāmahenoktā rājadharmāśritāḥ śubhāḥ dharmam āśramiṇāṃ śreṣṭhaṃ vaktum arhasi pārthiva
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: The auspicious duties pertaining to the dharma of kings have been declared by the Grandsire. Now, O lord, be pleased to speak of the highest dharma of those who dwell in the orders of life.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca sarvatra vihito dharmaḥ svargyaḥ satyaphalaṃ tapaḥ bahudvārasya dharmasya nehāsti viphalā kriyā
english: Bhīṣma said: Dharma is ordained everywhere, and leads to heaven; austerity has truth for its fruit. Of dharma, which has many gateways, no act here is fruitless.

sanskrit: yasmin yasmiṃs tu vinaye yo yo yāti viniścayam sa tam evābhijānāti nānyaṃ bharatasattama
english: Whatever discipline a man comes to settle upon, that very one he acknowledges and no other, O best of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: yathā yathā ca paryeti lokatantram asāravat tathā tathā virāgo 'tra jāyate nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: And the more one comes to grasp how the fabric of the world is without substance, the more does dispassion toward it arise—of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: evaṃ vyavasite loke bahudoṣe yudhiṣṭhira ātmamokṣanimittaṃ vai yateta matimān naraḥ
english: Since the world is found to be thus full of faults, O Yudhiṣṭhira, a man of understanding should strive for the sake of the liberation of his self.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca naṣṭe dhane vā dāre vā putre pitari vā mṛte yayā buddhyā nudec chokaṃ tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: When wealth is lost, or a wife, or when a son or a father has died, by what understanding may one drive away grief? Tell me that, O Grandsire.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca naṣṭe dhane vā dāre vā putre pitari vā mṛte aho duḥkham iti dhyāyañ śokasyāpacitiṃ caret
english: Bhīṣma said: When wealth is lost, or a wife, or when a son or a father has died, brooding "Ah, the sorrow of it!"—thus one should work toward the wearing away of grief.

sanskrit: atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam yathā senajitaṃ vipraḥ kaś cid ity abravīd vacaḥ
english: On this point too they relate this ancient tale of how a certain brāhmaṇa spoke these words to Senajit.
